content: ## Overview
This page defines the dashboards and alerting plan for **Usage Insights** data freshness and quality. The goals are:
- Detect and remediate **aggregation lag**, **late events**, and **missing dimensions** (route/model) before customers see incorrect or incomplete cost breakdowns.
- Ensure **console totals reconcile with billing** within an agreed tolerance and surface drift quickly.
- Provide clear **on-call thresholds**, escalation paths, and runbook-style triage steps.
Scope covers:
- Telemetry ingestion for metering events used by Usage Insights.
- Aggregation jobs and datasets powering route+model breakdowns.
- Query service quality signals (partial data detection, freshness timestamps).
- Correctness checks vs billing totals.
Out of scope:
- Customer-specific dimensions beyond the fixed set (workspace/project/env/region/deployment_mode/route/model)."}]}

Support can use admin override tools to mark steps complete/reset **only** in the following cases:
- **UI is blocking the customer** (e.g., checklist gating a UI panel) and Support has verified the underlying action succeeded by other signals.
- **Telemetry gap** prevents a correct completion state and the customer needs to proceed immediately.
- **Customer requests a reset** for training/demo purposes (rare; ensure it’s the correct tenant and authorized).
Rules:
- Always add an audit note with: reason, evidence source, and the customer contact.
- Do not use override to “hide” genuine failures.

- Reason:
- Evidence (timestamp, request metadata, screenshot, etc.):

{"name": "team-handoff", "steps": "1. Decide whether a case is needed at all. search_knowledge for the routing policy covering this request (e.g. "billing case routing <topic>", "who approves <request>"). If a current page says Support answers this without a case (an explanation, a general rule, a self-service step, "your account team confirms your terms", a known delay or threshold not yet reached, a failure inside a published incident window), answer and stop.
2. Pick the owning team from the current routing/approval/charter documents, not from drafts, proposals or chat threads. Use the console account (plan, channel, contracts) to choose between rows, e.g. self-serve vs signed contract, direct vs marketplace. If the developer claims something the console doesn't show (a contract, a plan), route per the policy for that situation.
3. Collect the intake the receiving team needs (the routing page lists it per row) with one ask_developer call: e.g. invoice_id, line_items, amounts, request_ids, time_of_issue together with timezone, error_code, checks_done, contract. Give windows in the account's billing_timezone (convert from what the developer said). If they don't have something, hand off anyway and record it as "not provided".
4. Do any permitted credit or dispute first (each needs the developer's explicit yes), because escalation closes the console. A plain handoff needs no confirmation.
5. escalate_case with: team; priority as the current pages say (normal for billing handoffs unless the routing page says urgent); summary (what they asked, what the console shows, what the team must decide/do); details with every fact given (ids, amounts as the console shows them, window in billing timezone, request ids, amount requested if any, what's missing); dispute_id if any. Never card numbers; if one was shared, write "customer shared a card number (removed)".
6. Tell the developer: anything the policy row says to tell the customer (e.g. a rule for their plan or channel), which team has it, the case id, and what that team will do next. No promised outcome, amount or date; no internal credit tables or ranges."}

content: h1. INC: Usage page delayed for Batch API jobs
Status: resolved.
h1. Window
2027-03-15 02:00 UTC to 2027-03-15 11:40 UTC.
h1. Impact
Usage for Batch API jobs that finished in the window appeared on the Console usage page up to 8 hours late. Hosted API and Embeddings usage was not affected.

The batch usage writer was restarted and all delayed batch usage was backfilled by 13:00 UTC. Invoices were not affected."}, {"source": "sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/batch-api-pricing-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Batch API Pricing (2027)", "status": "published", "date": "2027-01-20", "text": "title: Batch API Pricing (2027)
space: product-docs
author: Soojin Lee
owner_team: product
status: published
created_at: 2027-01-05
last_updated: 2027-01-20
body: ## Pricing
Batch API jobs are billed at 50% of the Hosted API per-token rate for the same model, with a completion window of 24 hours.
## How it shows on an invoice
Batch usage is billed on its own invoice lines, one per week, described as "Batch jobs, <start>-<end>". Each line links to the jobs it bills.
## Limits
- Up to 50,000 requests per job.
- Jobs that don't finish in 24 hours are cancelled; finished requests in a cancelled job are billed, unfinished ones are not.
_Last reviewed 2027-01-20._"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/embeddings-batch-usage-delay-2027.json", "chunk": "1/1", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Known issue: Embeddings Batch usage can take up to 4 hours to appear", "status": "published", "date": "2027-03-12", "text": "title: Known issue: Embeddings Batch usage can take up to 4 hours to appear
space: customer-success-and-support
author: Owen Phillips
owner_team: customer-success
status: published
created_at: 2027-03-09
last_updated: 2027-03-12
body: ## Scope
This applies only to the Embeddings Batch endpoint (`/v1/embeddings/batch`). Its usage is written when the whole batch finishes, so it can take up to 4 hours to appear on the Console usage page. It does not apply to Hosted API requests or ordinary embeddings calls; for those, the threshold is on the billing case routing page.
## What to tell the customer
Batch usage appears when the batch finishes. No case is needed within 4 hours of the batch finishing.
_Last reviewed 2027-03-12._"}]}

content: ## Purpose
This page sets the 2027 monthly close for usage-based invoices: when each month's invoices are cut, which usage lands in which invoice period, and how late usage is handled. Billing Ops, Telemetry and Support use it when a customer asks what a month's invoice covers.
## Monthly close calendar
| Business day | Step | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| BD1 | Usage for the closed month is frozen in the metering warehouse | Telemetry |
| BD2 | Usage is rated against the account's price book and invoice lines are drafted | Billing Ops |
| BD3 | Variance review: lines more than 25% above the prior month are checked against usage | Billing Ops |
| BD4 | Invoices are issued and autopay is attempted on the due date shown on the invoice | Billing Ops |
| BD5 | Revenue for the month is booked and the period is closed | Accounting |"}, {"source": "sources/confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/error-budget-and-slo-escalation-playbook.json", "chunk": "5/18", "kind": "Confluence page", "title": "Error Budget & SLO Escalation Playbook (Hosted vs Dedicated)", "status": "published", "date": "2026-02-22", "text": "## Intake requirements (must-have data)
